name: Bright Owusu

professionalSummary.short: Bright Omari Owusu is an early-career software engineer studying computer science and cybersecurity at Grambling State University. His work spans backend systems, cloud infrastructure, application security, developer tooling, and AI automation, with recent projects centered on Cloudflare authentication, deterministic code generation, AWS networking, and security checks inside code review.
professionalSummary.throughLine: He tends to turn manual or fragile engineering work into testable systems: security triage becomes an agent workflow, HTML migration becomes a deterministic compiler, authentication becomes a reusable service, and scanner output becomes part of pull-request review.
differentiators: Combines software construction with security review instead of treating security as a final checklist.
Works across application code, infrastructure, automation, and deployment boundaries.
Uses AI where it helps, but also builds deterministic systems when predictability matters more.
Documents limitations and verification status instead of polishing every experiment into a product claim.

education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Cybersecurity

highlights: Audited an internal AI system and presented six critical excessive-permission and prompt-injection findings that drove a rebuild.
Cut on-call response time from six minutes to 30 seconds for more than 2,000 engineers by building a Vertex AI agent that retrieved from BigQuery, Jira, and internal security playbooks through Slack.
Achieved 90% tool-call accuracy across 400 threads by engineering deterministic Python middleware between model calls.
Scaled a retrieval corpus to 327 documents through a pipeline that validated, synthesized, and ingested Slack data.
Migrated Terraform workflows to Pulumi and Python and built a dynamic provider for declarative retrieval-corpus management.
Automated competitor price tracking across more than 65 websites with an ETL pipeline that processed more than one million daily product records into Google Sheets.
Reduced market-intelligence research from hours to under two minutes with a model-agnostic n8n workflow.
Deployed a LiteLLM router for Gemini and Mistral that reduced per-inference cost from $0.17 to $0.07.
Merged more than 100 pull requests supporting more than 300 users, backed by more than 70 PyTest integration tests for ride-booking workflows.
Removed double-assignment race conditions affecting about 15 rides per week by moving driver claims into one atomic update.
Reduced infrastructure cost by 30% by migrating ride endpoints from EC2 to DigitalOcean with a blue-green cutover.
Red-teamed an AWS Bedrock agent with a 180-prompt injection corpus targeting privilege escalation.
Reduced successful escalations from 34% to 4% by binding token audience to user intent.
Researched least-privilege IAM patterns for data in agent sessions and documented the model selected for deployment.
Developed a Zero Trust IAM framework for security gaps between static accounts and dynamic agents.
Presented the findings to faculty in terms of reusable security principles.

projects.name: Immigration Assistant
projects.status: Public project website; beta application access is described as coming soon
projects.problem: Help users explore immigration information, status records, and employer research while keeping sensitive data out of external embedding services.
highlights: Led three engineers on a retrieval pipeline over more than 500,000 lines of USCIS policy.
Reported 88% accuracy on a human-annotated set of 200 questions and answers.
Generated embeddings on-device with TensorFlow to keep personally identifiable information away from external services.
Separated the application source from the public landing-page repository.
limits: The public URL is the project website, not proof that every application feature is live.
The website retains external assets and template-derived browser behavior.

projects.name: Uncluster
projects.subtitle: HTML, untangled
projects.problem: Convert HTML exports into editable React or Express/EJS projects without asking a language model to guess the structure.
highlights: Uses more than 70 deterministic attribute-translation rules and depth-first component extraction.
Separates CSS and JavaScript, collects page assets, and emits editable project structures.
Exposes a command-line tool, API, and browser interface.
Includes remote-destination checks and download limits.
limits: It preserves page structure instead of inferring application behavior.
Generated components, dependencies, and asset rights still need review.
The tool does not establish permission to copy a website.

projects.name: WVS
projects.subtitle: Bringing security findings into code review
projects.problem: Make scanner output easier to import, review, explain, and act on during a pull-request workflow.
highlights: Combines scan results, pull-request imports, finding exports, and AI-assisted explanations.
Integrates four static-analysis tools into a GitHub Actions trigger.
Reported more than 50 findings and 12 flags across 25 test codebases.
Keeps proposed remediation subject to human review.
limits: The repository is an attempt, not a production scanner service.
The GitHub Actions workflow covers changes under sandbox/, not every repository path.
A skipped scanner check is not a passing scan.
